He saw the settlement at first light, a scatter of gray roofs in a fold of the sage, and he drew rein on the ridge to study it. Smoke rose from only two chimneys. The corrals were empty. Something was wrong — he could feel it in the way his horse tossed its head — and he sat for a long time with his hand resting on the saddle horn, thinking. A hawk wheeled overhead. At last he nudged the horse forward, down the stony slope, his rifle laid across his knees. The wind carried the smell of cold ashes to him; and under it, faintly, the sound of someone weeping.
